Contents roadmap only. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Right-hand rule figure and F vector = I vector cross B vector viewed. The text explicitly defines F as force per unit length, not total force. A conductor need not translate macroscopically to experience force; moving charge/current suffices. General straight-conductor force includes length and sine of field angle. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

DC/AC classification, force F=BIL and a length-L conductor figure. Scalar law assumes perpendicular conductor and uniform field. Moving-conductor induced EMF requires the appropriate nonzero flux-cutting component. Broad modern-DC prevalence is context dependent and differs from the later industrial AC-servo summary. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Faraday equation e=−dφ/dt and Lenz explanation. Printed phrase oppose the charge producing it is a typo; following text refers correctly to change in flux. One-turn flux versus total flux linkage must be declared. Not every induced EMF is a motor back EMF. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Two rotating-loop diagrams, N left/S right, active-side opposing forces form a couple. Current reversal at the vertical passage sustains torque sense. Zero resultant force can coexist with nonzero torque. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Slotted armature, field poles, segmented commutator, carbon brushes and four-pole diagram viewed. Coil-current switching sustains rotation. Reversing armature current or field current alone reverses electromagnetic torque; reversing both does not. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

PM constant-flux model, F=BIL, effective N conductors F=NBIL, T=Fb=NBILb=Kt I and Vb=Kvω. Figure labels L and active-side separation b. N is the source effective conductor factor, not an invitation to count both sides twice. Kv here is a back-EMF constant, not rpm/V speed constant. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Series equivalent circuit R,L,Vb, neglected-inductance current (V−Kvω)/R, torque Kt(V−Kvω)/R. Torque-speed lines for V2>V1 and current-torque linear plot inspected. Zero-load zero-torque is the ideal no-loss model; physical no-load friction needs torque/current. Initial zero-speed proportional torque is quasi-steady, not instantaneous current jump with nonzero inductance. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Series-wound circuit and qualitative curves. Reversing supply reverses armature and field together. Under unsaturated flux proportional to current, torque is proportional to current squared; the displayed convex-up current-versus-torque plot does not quantitatively match that model. Unloaded overspeed is a risk, not a recommended experiment. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Shunt parallel-field prose, starting/regulation/reversal points and curves. Drawing places Ra/La before the field branch, unlike the usual independent shunt field and armature branch; preserve as a source topology issue rather than teach it as a wiring schematic. Constant-flux torque proportional to armature current is not the displayed curved current-torque plot. Near-constant speed is approximate, not exact load independence. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Compound series/shunt prose, circuit, three torque-speed curves and full comparison table. Prose says highest starting torque while table labels compound average, a direct local conflict. Table shunt high field resistance/good controllability/average start; series low/poor/high; compound high parallel and low series/average/average. Qualitative comparison, not a universal motor rating. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

PM motor cutaway labels encoder, commutator, magnet, ironless winding, brush, reduction gearhead and output shaft. PM field does not imply brushless. No field excitation power is needed, but winding/friction and drive losses remain. Relative efficiency and torque/weight claims are design dependent. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Speed-control prose and PWM pulse figure inspected. PM current determines torque within the linear model; speed also depends on voltage/back EMF/load. PWM varies average applied voltage at fixed supply. A duty ratio is not generally the same percentage of loaded speed. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

H bridge S1 upper-left, S2 upper-right, S3 lower-left, S4 lower-right. Diagonals S1/S4 and S2/S3 reverse motor voltage; same-leg simultaneous conduction shorts the rail. Source BJT A/B drive example and freewheel diodes inspected. Base terminology is BJT-specific; dead time and current paths need engineering design, not this simplified sketch. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Two full feedback diagrams viewed: forward digital controller→DAC→analogue amplifier→motor in both; tachogenerator analogue feedback→ADC→controller above; encoder digital→code converter→controller below. Encoder replaces the analogue feedback conversion, not the pictured forward DAC. Feedback alone does not guarantee stability. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

BLDC diagram shows permanent-magnet rotor N/S and stator coil sectors A,B,C,D. Electronic sequential coil switching replaces brush/commutator wear and sparking. Three sensors are the illustrated sensored implementation, not a universal requirement. The last line mentions base current, specific to the transistor example. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Full tree inspected: single-phase low-power and polyphase high-power branches each divide into induction and synchronous. Relative cost/control-difficulty assertions are broad historical/general statements, not specification rules. Frequency sets synchronous field speed; induction rotor speed also depends on slip. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Induction motor as transformer: stationary primary/stator, rotating secondary/rotor, air gap. The text broadly says AC motor rotor power is induced; the heading and mechanism apply to induction motors, not every synchronous AC motor. Brushed DC conduction statement does not define all brushless DC variants. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Cage diagram and text: copper/aluminium bars and end rings close rotor circuits; no external rotor electrical connection; stator windings driven by AC. Ideal single main-winding rotor at rest has zero net starting torque, hence auxiliary starting methods. This is not a claim that every packaged single-phase motor lacks a start arrangement. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

PM synchronous rotor and stator winding diagram. One pole-pair example rotates one mechanical turn per electrical cycle. More pole pairs reduce mechanical speed at fixed frequency. PM rotor is an example, not every synchronous machine. Bare fixed-frequency starting difficulty does not exclude inverter-controlled startup. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Stepper PM rotor and two perpendicular winding axes W1/W2 diagram inspected. Pulse count sets nominal position and pulse rate speed, conditional on no missed steps. Full list 12,24,72,144,180,200 steps per turn corresponds to 30,15,5,2.5,2,1.8 degrees. PM versus variable-reluctance is the presented classification, not exhaustive of hybrid designs. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

VR rotor is ferromagnetic, aligns to low reluctance/high flux. Diagram shows eight stator poles A,A-prime through D,D-prime and six rotor teeth, with A/A-prime excited. Phase means independent stator winding, not individual tooth count. Step angle is per specified switching transition. Powered holding torque differs from unpowered detent torque; the source reversing-spindle clause is not a separate definition requirement. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Six selection factors: speed range, torque-speed variation, reversibility, duty cycle, starting torque, power. Servo graph has distinct driver-peak, motor-continuous and commutation-limit curves. At 2000 rpm and about 1 N m a point is above the continuous boundary but below the peak curve; do not infer continuous suitability from a peak rating. Plot is illustrative, not a motor datasheet or exact numeric specification. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Operating point is motor/load torque-curve intersection. Declining motor curve and rising load curve depicted. Self-regulation follows their local slope relation under a positive-inertia mechanical model; not every arbitrary intersection is stable. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Below pictured equilibrium motor torque exceeds load and accelerates; above it load exceeds motor and decelerates. Changing supplied voltage shifts the motor characteristic and equilibrium. Generic source claim needs an admissible stable operating point and operating limits. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Accuracy is possible not guaranteed, and microstep command resolution is not actual accuracy. Categories overlap: coreless is construction, servo is a controlled system. The introduction lists nonlinear friction, backlash, cable flexibility, compliance and contact among difficult effects. Learning targets include forward/inverse dynamics and residuals. Adaptation requires data and an update mechanism; it is not automatic. Printed footer 3 inspected separately. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Full equation M(Θ)Θddot+C(Θ,Θdot)+G(Θ)=τ. C is the Coriolis/centrifugal generalized-force vector in this notation, not an unmultiplied n×n matrix. All position/velocity/acceleration/M/C/G/τ definitions inspected. Inverse map takes positions, velocities and accelerations to torque; feedforward/computed torque/tracking applications. No explicit friction/contact term in the displayed nominal equation. Footer 4. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Forward dynamics input (Θ,Θdot,τ), output acceleration, Θddot=M inverse(τ−C−G). Applications simulation, RL, MPC, digital twins. Motion requires integration after instantaneous acceleration; invertibility/model scope declared. Footer 5. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

All approximation, data-driven and differentiability bullets were inspected, together with the box naming Deep Lagrangian, Hamiltonian and physics-informed networks. Representation capacity and derivative availability do not establish trained accuracy. Printed footer 6 inspected separately. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Forward 2R diagram: six inputs θ1 θ2 θdot1 θdot2 τ1 τ2, two illustrative 32-neuron hidden layers, ReLU/tanh labels, two acceleration outputs. Arm diagram θ1 relative horizontal, θ2 relative first-link extension, lengths l1/l2 and masses m1 at elbow,m2 distal; torques τ1/τ2. Footer 7. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Phase 1 specifies an MLP with widths 6–30–20–2, sigmoid activation and backpropagation. Nominal synthetic data span beyond the physical operating region. The reported 1.5 million iterations and average error below 5% are experiment-specific, not a universal stop guarantee or permission to exceed real actuator limits. Printed footer 8 inspected separately. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

Phase 2 uses bounded sinusoidal torques, frequencies below half the joint natural frequency and an example cap of 5 Hz. It reports 58,000 samples at 5 ms intervals, then 100 fine-tuning iterations. Validation uses novel torque inputs, ODE integration and real-motion comparison. The sample rate is 200 Hz; endpoint span is 289.995 s under consecutive sampling. Printed footer 9 inspected separately. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

The2R inverse-dynamics example has l1=l2=1 m, m1=m2=1 kg as point masses at the link tips, and g=9.81 m/s². MLP regression takes joint positions, velocities and accelerations to two torques. The figure measures θ1 from horizontal and θ2 from the first-link extension. Its input box interleaves joint triples, unlike the later grouped code order. The learned predictor need not expose parameters at inference, but synthetic label generation uses known parameters. Footer10. Actual 1800×1013 pixels inspected alongside text.

The printed mass matrix has M11=(m1+m2)l1²+m2l2²+2m1l1l2cosθ2, M12=M21=m2l2²+m2l1l2cosθ2, and M22=m2l2². The cross term in M11 prints m1, but the illustrated distal point-mass model requires m2. The ordered input is [q1,q2,q̇1,q̇2,q̈1,q̈2], with two torque targets. Angles span ±π, velocities ±2π and accelerations ±10. There are 50,000 independent random state tuples. Footer11. Training-data bias in CV/NLP; uneven face/speech performance across demographic groups; physical consequences; fairness testing within validation. No numeric dataset or preferred fairness metric provided.

Footer17. E-stop independent of AI software/hang; proximity zones slow then stop; redundant independent sensing limits one-sensor failure. Independence and diagnostic coverage are assumptions, not guaranteed by merely duplicating a sensor.

Footer18. RL out-of-distribution behavior, confidently wrong perception, sim-to-real dynamics mismatch, reduced interpretability versus PID/LQR. Opening contrast does not mean conventional control has no uncertainty or OOD failure.

Footer19. Classical safety-envelope override; confidence monitoring/conservative fallback; domain randomization; human override for high-consequence decisions.
